identity.name: Launggyet Kingdom
native_names: လောင်းကြက်

land.text: northern Arakan in the Kaladan valley: 'located in present-day northern Rakhine State', without Sandoway (Thandwe), which stayed independent until 1437

successors.note: Min Saw Mon, proclaimed at Launggyet on 18 April 1429, founds Mrauk U; the mrauk-u dossier starts in April 1429 with counterpart 'Launggyet (Pegu's nominee)'.

capitals.name: Launggyet
capitals.note: 'The capital, Launggyet, was strategically situated in the Kaladan River valley.' The page gives no moves; Mrauk U was founded on 16 November 1430.

correction.text: northern Arakan in the Kaladan valley: 'located in present-day northern Rakhine State', without Sandoway (Thandwe), which stayed independent until 1437

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Arakan row between its Chandra Dynasty, ending 1055, and its Kingdom of Mrauk U, from 1429): the Mrauk U 1429 shape (84,574 km2) without the Sandoway district, which the kingdom 'was still restricted to' in 1429. The Launggyet page gives no frontier or area. The shape holds in outline through Ava's occupation of 1406-1408 and Pegu's tributary years 1412-1421 (a change of overlord, not of land).

region.text: northern Arakan in the Kaladan valley: 'located in present-day northern Rakhine State', without Sandoway (Thandwe), which stayed independent until 1437

ledger.note: 1237: Alawmaphyu Min founds the Launggyet dynasty on the Kaladan. 'The dynasty was founded in 1237 by King Alawmaphyu Min after the fall of Vesali' (the Rakhine Razawin Thit gives 22 April 1251); it 'succeeded the Vesali kingdom'. Pagan's ledger counts Arakan its tributary 1066-1287; this page does not.

region.text: northern Arakan in the Kaladan valley: 'located in present-day northern Rakhine State', without Sandoway (Thandwe), which stayed independent until 1437

ledger.note: 29 November 1406: Ava overruns Launggyet. 'Ava troops overran Launggyet on 29 November 1406'; Minkhaung I sent the crown prince Minye Kyawswa and 'appointed Anawrahta Saw, then governor of Kalay, to be king of Arakan'; Min Saw Mon 'barely escaped to Chittagong'. The Launggyet page dates the sack to 1404.

region.text: northern Arakan in the Kaladan valley: 'located in present-day northern Rakhine State', without Sandoway (Thandwe), which stayed independent until 1437

ledger.note: 1408: Pegu dislodges Ava from Arakan. 'In 1408, Peguan forces dislodged Avan troops from Arakan.' Arakan 'was to be a battlefield between Ava and Pegu for the next six years' (Min Saw Mon page); Ava held an outpost at Khwethin-Taung in North Arakan in 1413-1416.

region.text: northern Arakan in the Kaladan valley: 'located in present-day northern Rakhine State', without Sandoway (Thandwe), which stayed independent until 1437

ledger.note: 18 April 1429: Min Saw Mon is proclaimed king at Launggyet and the dynasty gives way to Mrauk U. 'Saw Mon was proclaimed king at Launggyet on 18 April 1429' after a February-March invasion with Bengal's help; he founded Mrauk-U on 16 November 1430. The Launggyet page: 'By 1430, the Launggyet dynasty came to an end as Mrauk U emerged as the new political and cultural center of Arakan.'

wars.name: Ava's conquest of Arakan (Forty Years' War)

zones.text: northern Arakan in the Kaladan valley: 'located in present-day northern Rakhine State', without Sandoway (Thandwe), which stayed independent until 1437

wars.outcome: Ava overran Launggyet on 29 November 1406 and installed a nominee; Pegu dislodged the Avan troops in 1408; Arakan was Pegu's tributary 1412-1421 and Min Saw Mon returned in 1429.
wars.note: The Forty Years' War page dates the Ava conquest of Launggyet '1404-1406'; the Min Saw Mon page gives 29 November 1406.

certainty.note: Chronicle history; the pages name a river valley and a capital, not a frontier.

notes: State Cliopatria lacks; named by se-01-d, se-01-f and se-01-c. Three pages opened. Not settled: (1) the founding is 1237 or 22 April 1251 on one page; the rulers are only partly listed (Min Hti 1279-1374, a 95-year reign the page calls legendary), so no ruler strip; (2) pagan-kingdom counts Arakan its tributary 1066-1287 (counterpart 'arakan'), which begins 170 years before the Launggyet dynasty and is not on the Launggyet page: the Arakan of 1056-1236 (between the Chandra Dynasty row, ending 1055, and Launggyet) has no dossier; (3) the Launggyet page dates Ava's sack to 1404, the Min Saw Mon page to 29 November 1406 (used); ava-kingdom's occupation_end 1408 is confirmed by the Forty Years' War page, while Arakan stayed a battlefield to 1412; (4) from 1373/74 Launggyet's court took nominees from Ava, which is overlordship not drawn here; Pegu's 1412-1421 tribute is carried by hanthawaddy-kingdom's vassal pair; (5) Sandoway (Thandwe), independent to 1437, needs a dossier if the orchestrator wants it (suggested slug sandoway).
